answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active association worker and 3 inactive workers, draws 8 Zoo cards and keeps 4, and draws 2 Final Scoring cards. Each of the five Action cards starts side I up; Animals is placed in the leftmost slot (strength 1), and the other four are placed randomly in the remaining slots. Appeal starts staggered by turn order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Setup D: Take 25 money; E: Draw 2 Final Scoring cards; F: Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4. Action cards: side I up, Animals under the leftmost slot; remaining 4 randomly. Appeal track: start player on 0, second on 1, third on 2, fourth on 3. C3: 1 active worker and remaining 3 lying down.

answers.answer: Four-player games place 4 Base Conservation Project cards face up; games with fewer players place 3. Only a 2-player game blocks spaces: one level on each face-up base project (left level on the left card, middle on the middle card, right on the right card) and the three spaces in the left column of the donation area are blocked for both players. Thus there are no such blocked spaces in 3- or 4-player games. The initial six-card display is revealed after everyone has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b: ‘In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up ...; otherwise the 3 topmost.’ Setup 5c says ‘2-player game only’ and specifies the three blocked project levels and donation spaces. Setup G: ‘After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.’

answers.answer: After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were to its left one slot to the right, and put the used card in slot 1. Action strength is set before the action; each X-token spent then adds 1 strength, and you may spend any number (though some actions stop benefiting above strength 5). X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action, and you may hold at most 5. Effects marked ‘after finishing’ resolve after the action is complete, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1.’ X-tokens: ‘each token spent adds +1 strength’ and strength is set before acting; max 5 held. ‘After finishing’ effects occur after completing the action, including moving Action cards.

answers.answer: You may not do nothing: playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not legal, and the alternative X-token action is for when you cannot or do not want to perform a regular action. Choose an Action card, move it to slot 1, and shift the intervening cards right; its strength and upgrade state do not matter. Take exactly 1 X-token. You cannot use this action if you already have 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘You may not do nothing’; use the alternative X-token action when you cannot or do not want a regular action. X-token action: take exactly 1, move the selected card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards; strength and upgrade state are irrelevant; unavailable at 5 tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any extra steps beyond that space. The player whose action/effect reached it gains 1 X-token, and the break happens after that player's current turn ends. The triggering player completes the turn; then the break occurs. After the break, play continues clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: ‘When it reaches the last space, you call a break for everyone: the break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get 1 X-token ... Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space.’ Break procedure: ‘Play then continues clockwise with the next player.’

answers.answer: Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck according to the card's strength table (up to 3, possibly discarding one) or snaps exactly 1 display card at strength 5 or more, regardless of reputation. Cards II also advances the token 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or from within reputation range in any order; it uses the upgraded table. Its snap threshold is strength 3, and strength above 3 does not improve a snap; display cards for this upgraded action are limited to reputation range. Cards taken from the display are not replenished until the turn is complete. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard to 3 cards (or 5 with the relevant university) at breaks.
answers.evidence: Cards I: ‘Advance the Break token 2 spaces’; draw up to the indicated number (maximum 3) or snap at strength 5+ regardless of reputation. Cards II: advance 2, draw from deck and/or within reputation range; snap from strength 3. Display is replenished at turn end. ‘There is no in-turn hand limit; you only discard to your limit during breaks.’

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card on the folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10 or higher requires the upgraded Cards action. At space 15, each additional reputation step gives 1 appeal while the counter remains at 15. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: ‘Within reputation range’ means the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at space 15, further reputation gives 1 appeal per step. ‘You may not look through the discard pile during the game.’

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building, of size no greater than the action strength, at 2 money per space, paid before placing it. Build II may build multiple different buildings whose total size is no greater than strength, but never two identical buildings in one action. Your first building must have at least one space on a map border; each later building must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Buildings must fit on empty spaces without overlap or extending off the map, and cannot cover water or rock. Restricted-icon spaces require upgraded Build. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately gives 1 appeal, once.
answers.evidence: Build I: ‘exactly 1 building ... size up to ... strength’ and ‘2 money per space.’ Placement rules specify first building on a border, later adjacency, empty spaces, water/rock and restricted-icon limits, and kiosk spacing. Each pavilion ‘increases your zoo's appeal by 1.’ Build II allows different buildings up to total strength, never 2 identical.

answers.answer: Build I offers kiosks, pavilions, standard enclosures of sizes 1–5, and the size-3 Petting Zoo (maximum 1 per zoo). Build II additionally offers the size-5 Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary (maximum 1 of each per zoo); each may be built only once per zoo. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every zoo-map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Build I lists kiosk, pavilion, standard enclosures, and Petting Zoo (maximum 1). Build II adds Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary, both size 5 and maximum 1 each. ‘Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.’ Full map grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. Association II tasks resolve in sequence, so workers or other bonuses gained on an earlier task can be used on a later task in that action. For a multi-building Build action, pay for each building separately before placing it and take placement bonuses before building the next; ‘after finishing’ bonuses wait until the entire action is complete. Animal effects other than ‘after finishing’ effects resolve immediately (including before another animal), while ‘after finishing’ waits until all animals are played and the Action card has moved to slot 1. For simultaneous effects, the owner chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-token section: ‘Bonuses gained earlier in an action ... may be used for later steps ... You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits.’ Build II specifies separate payment and immediate placement bonuses, with after-finishing effects held until the whole action. Animals section distinguishes immediate effects from after-finishing effects. Association II says earlier task bonuses may be used later; simultaneous effects are ordered by the owner.

answers.answer: For each animal, first meet all conditions on the card, then pay its full cost; a matching-continent partner zoo reduces the cost by 3 money per continent icon, so a double icon gives a 6-money reduction. Then house it: any animal other than a Petting Zoo animal may occupy its own empty standard enclosure of at least the required size; Petting Zoo animals must go in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use their special enclosure, marking the card's indicated number of spaces with player tokens, if capacity remains. Some animals require one or two adjacent water and/or rock spaces; count distinct adjacent hexes, and those requirements also apply when using a special enclosure. Standard enclosures flip to occupied; special enclosures never flip. Place the card and execute effects: appeal and other ordinary effects resolve immediately, while after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action ends. You must be able to pay the full cost before any money-gain effect from that play pays out.
answers.evidence: Animals I lists conditions, cost and the partner-zoo discount ‘3 money per continent icon,’ enclosure placement and water/rock requirements, special-enclosure capacity tokens, and effect timing. The money-timing rule says the full animal cost must be payable before gain-money effects pay out.

answers.answer: Animals II allows Animal cards from the display within reputation range, with an additional cost equal to the folder number; the two animals may be any mix of hand and display cards. Do not refill the display until the turn ends. At strength 5 or more, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, before determining display range. It also permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Animals II: play from the display within reputation range, pay the folder number, mix hand/display for two animals, and do not replenish until turn end. At strength 5+, reputation may increase by 1 ‘at the very beginning of the action.’ May play animals with the upgrade-required icon.

answers.answer: Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, and only once per building, may you move suitable existing animals from standard enclosures into it: reptiles and the birds eligible for the respective special enclosure. The summary gives no fixed number of animals; move suitable animals as capacity allows, marking the special enclosure with the number of spaces shown on each animal card using player tokens. For each animal moved, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all of that animal's requirements, including water/rock, back to empty. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even its size, flip none. Decide separately for each animal.
answers.evidence: Build II says moving suitable animals is immediate and ‘only once per building.’ Animal rules identify reptiles and some birds as eligible and mark required spaces with player tokens. The edge-case rule specifies the smallest standard enclosure meeting all requirements, fallback to smallest meeting size, otherwise none, decided per animal.

answers.answer: Association task strengths are: increase reputation 2, gain partner zoo 3, gain university 4, conservation project work 5. Side I performs exactly one task. Side II performs one or more different tasks whose total values do not exceed the action strength. Each task needs worker(s): if you already have one worker on that task, place 2 workers instead; if you already have 3 there, you cannot do that task again before the break. Other players' workers do not matter. Side II uses 1 or 2 of your workers per task under those same rules.
answers.evidence: Association I gives task strengths 2, 3, 4, 5 and says exactly one task; if 1 of your workers is there, place 2, and if 3 are there, wait until after break. ‘Other players' workers ... do not matter.’ Association II allows different tasks up to total strength, using 1 or 2 workers per task.

answers.answer: Take partner zoos and universities from the Association board and place each on the lowest available corresponding space on your zoo map; take any printed space bonus immediately, and take any reputation shown by a university. Partner zoos must represent different continents, you may have at most 4, and the third or fourth requires upgraded Association. You cannot take a duplicate university. Universities grant reputation and research icons; only a particular university raises the hand limit to 5 (otherwise it is 3 at breaks). At breaks, the supply is replenished so each zoo and university is available exactly once, except those all players already have.
answers.evidence: Association task text: take zoos/universities from the board onto the lowest empty spaces and take printed bonuses; zoos must be from different continents, max 4, third/fourth need upgraded Association; no duplicate universities. Universities grant reputation/research icons and are the only way to raise hand limit to 5. Break step 3 replenishes each exactly once, skipping items all players already have.

answers.answer: With Association I, conservation-project work either supports a project already in play or plays a Conservation Project card from hand and supports it immediately. Association II also allows the new card to come from the display within reputation range, paying the folder number, with no display refill until turn end. To support a project, fulfill a condition with no player token on it and place one player token of your choice from the left edge of your zoo map there; you may support a given project only once. Removing the token activates its zoo-map bonus immediately, and you choose whether to take that bonus before or after the project reward. If a new project exceeds the face-up project limit (2, 3, or 4 according to player count), discard the rightmost project; its tokens return to their owners' supplies, while their activated bonuses stay active. Base projects are not moved.
answers.evidence: Association project work describes supporting existing projects or playing from hand; Association II permits a display card within range for the folder cost. Support rules specify an unoccupied condition, one zoo-map token, once per project, and immediate bonus timing. Overflow discards the rightmost project and returns tokens to owners' supplies; base projects never move.

answers.answer: Yes. A Release into the Wild animal must require a standard enclosure of exactly the depicted size, neither smaller nor larger, even if it could also live in a special enclosure. Discarding it loses its printed appeal first, before gaining conservation points, and removes its icons; keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. To free space, first remove the animal's indicated special-enclosure tokens if possible; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements (including water/rock), or, if none does, the smallest meeting size alone; if no occupied enclosure meets size, flip none.
answers.evidence: Release rules: standard size must ‘match exactly’; lose only printed appeal before conservation points, discard animal and lose icons, but keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects. New project grants 1 reputation. Special tokens are removed first if possible; otherwise flip the smallest standard meeting requirements, with size-only fallback or none.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor card from hand if action strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Sponsors II can play one or more cards if action strength plus 1 is at least their total levels; X-tokens can raise strength beyond 5. Side II cards may come from hand or the display within reputation range, with folder number paid as an extra cost and no display refill until turn end. Resolve cards sequentially, fully resolving each card's instant effects (except after-finishing effects) before the next. If using the break-money option, Sponsors I advances the Break token by the action strength and pays that full amount of money even when only one step remains; Sponsors II pays twice that amount.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I: exactly 1 hand card at strength at least its level, or break movement equal to strength and that much money even if fewer steps are needed. Sponsors II: strength +1 must cover total levels; display cards within reputation range cost the folder number and are not replenished until turn end; effects resolve before the next card; break option pays money twice.

answers.answer: Break order: (1) discard down to hand limit, normally 3 or 5 with the relevant university; (2) return Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens on Action cards; (3) recall all workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; (4) discard display folders 1 and 2, move the rest down, and refill; (5) take income—appeal income, then kiosk income, then break-icon income on Sponsor cards and activated map bonuses; (6) reset the Break token. For each kiosk, get 1 money for every adjacent unique building, special enclosure (occupied or empty), occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count. If multiple players take display cards during income, refill the display after each player. Usually income is simultaneous; if effects require ordering, start with the break initiator (or affected player closest to them) and proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Break procedure enumerates the six steps and hand limits. Kiosk income lists qualifying adjacent buildings and says empty standard enclosures do not count while empty special enclosures do. Income text says ‘refill the display after each player’ and gives the ordering rule if effects require it.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation points, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token by that space (if available). At 10, the first player to reach it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, all discard one before scoring. The game end is checked at the end of your own turn or during a break, when your Appeal and Conservation counters are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your turn ends or a break for this check. The triggering player finishes their turn and everyone else takes one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation points. Victory Points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player who supported the most conservation projects, then tied players share the victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring section gives the rewards at 2, 5, 8, and 10; end condition and check timing, delayed other-turn appeal, and additional turns; Final Scoring cap of 4 per card; VP formula and tiebreaks.
